exposure: planned home vaginal births after cesarean (VBACs)
cohort: 13,144 multiparous women, including 1,052 with a prior cesarean, who planned a VBAC at home with midwives contributing data to the Midwives Alliance of North America Statistics Project 2.0 cohort during 2004-2009.
finding: Women planning a home VBAC had a high likelihood of vaginal birth but experienced higher rates of transfer, blood loss, maternal postpartum infections, uterine rupture, and neonatal intensive care unit admissions compared to those without a prior cesarean.
mod_finding: Women with a prior cesarean who planned a home birth had a high likelihood of vaginal birth, but higher rates of transfer, and increased risks of complications like blood loss, infection, uterine rupture, and neonatal intensive care unit admissions.
